why: Like-for-like memory and CPU comparison of excise, Preview, Chrome and Acrobat. Every app is driven by the SAME real keystrokes (the only driver all of them accept; Chrome additionally gets ONE click in its page pane, see clickToFocus) and measured from OUTSIDE the process, summed over every process the app owns. excise's in-app runner (#1497) cannot drive the other two; its driving-fidelity check showed keystrokes do the same render work.

documents.why: 6 light pages: the fixed cost of having any document open
126 text-heavy pages: fonts, text, many pages
17 pages, 122 MB, image-heavy with transparency and CMYK: the worst case for image decode
20 pages, one 200 dpi JPEG each, no text: the common real-world scanned document
455 pages, 7 MB: the long-document regime (page index, thumbnails, text index) that 126 pages does not reach

20 copies of a dense CAD drawing: thousands of vector paths per page, so this stresses the path rasteriser where altona and scan stress image decode. Caveat: the 20 pages share ONE content stream, so an app that caches by object may render pages 2-20 cheaper than a real 20-page drawing
6 pages of a real AcroForm (state-ds11 passport application): widget and appearance-stream rendering

excise.name: excise
excise.why: Page Down is excise's next-page key (verified: 30 presses -> page 31). Isolated HOME with a seeded window.json fixes the window size; the default view is continuous.

preview.name: Preview
preview.why: Option-Down is Preview's next-page key; Page Down only scrolls one screen (verified: 3 Page Downs -> page 2, 3 Option-Downs -> +3 pages). Opened with `open -F` so no window state is restored.

chrome.name: Google Chrome
chrome.why: Chrome's built-in PDF viewer (PDFium). Launched with a FRESH --user-data-dir (Chrome restores tabs and PDF state from its profile: the same leak that made #1497's first calibration measure nothing) plus --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check. It opens at its own defaults, thumbnail sidebar shown, as Preview and Acrobat are measured at theirs. Quit through the menu: Cmd+Q shows a 'hold to quit' warning instead of quitting. clickToFocus: on open Chrome's keyboard focus is NOT in the page pane (Right/Left then step THUMBNAILS and Home/End/Up/PageUp do nothing: the first n=1 round of 2026-09-21 ran in that state). ONE click in the page pane, as a user makes, fixes it. Verified on irs after the click: Right = +1 page per press (10 presses -> 11), Left = -1, End -> 126, Home -> 1. Its page label names the page dominating the viewport, so at the end of a document whose last page is much larger than the rest (Altona) it reads pages-1: tolerated at end-of-document only (tolerated_end).

acrobat.name: Adobe Acrobat
acrobat.why: Acrobat 26 in Reader mode. Its page box shows the PAGE LABEL from /PageLabels, not the physical page (the 455-page book reads i / 7 / 446 for physical 1 / 31 / 455), so expected values come from the PDF (shown_page). Its left/right arrows are consumed by a focused AcroForm field (nextPageByDoc: Page Down on ds11, confirmed by a passing retry). The first open of a heavy document can be slow and ignore keys (settleByDoc on scan). Its UI is an embedded browser (AcroCEF) plus system WebKit processes, so the per-app process sum matters more here than anywhere. See DRIVING NOTES in scripts/reader_bench.py before changing any of it.

multiDocument.why: OPTIONAL set, run only with --multi (reader_bench.py and reader_speed_bench.py). What a second and a third open document cost, how much comes back when one closes, what three open documents burn at idle, and how fast switching between two draws. The single-document rows above stay the primary comparison.
multiDocument.systemTabbing: macOS 'Prefer tabs when opening documents' (defaults -g AppleWindowTabbingMode; absent means fullscreen). The bench READS it and never changes it. Under 'always' a window-mode app turns its new windows into native tabs, so the expected layout becomes tabs. The observed window count decides, and a mismatch fails the run.

windows.why: Cmd+` cycles an app's windows (system shortcut)

tabs.why: Ctrl+Tab selects the next tab in excise's own tabs, AppKit native tabs and Acrobat

configs.why: Preferences > Documents > Open Documents In = NewWindow, seeded into the isolated HOME's window.json
Open Documents In = NewTab: one window, excise's own tab strip (#1554)
Preview opens a window per document; they become native tabs only under the system setting, which is recorded, not changed
Acrobat opens documents as tabs of one window by default
